name: Maun Centre and the Mall
tagline: The tar road through town, with the shops and the bank
description: The functional centre strung along the main road, with the Ngami Centre and Nandos mall, the supermarkets, the banks and the safari operators' offices. It is not attractive but it is where everything practical happens, and it is where anyone staying long does their shopping and their admin.
bestFor: Anyone who needs supermarkets, banks and the safari offices close by
pros: All shops, banks and services in one place
cons: Traffic on the single main road

name: Thamalakane Riverfront
tagline: Along the river, where the lodges and the good houses are
description: The strip following the Thamalakane river northeast of the centre, where most of the lodges, guest farms and the better houses sit under big trees with the water in front of them. Hippos and elephants come through. It is the pleasant side of Maun and where almost every foreigner ends up.
bestFor: Almost anyone staying more than a few days
pros: River frontage with genuine wildlife passing
Lodges, restaurants and the sociable end of town
Shaded and cooler than the centre
cons: Hippos and elephants are a real hazard at night

name: Maun Airport Area
tagline: Around the airstrip, where the light aircraft leave from
description: The district around Maun's airport, which handles an extraordinary volume of light aircraft for a town this size because every delta camp is reached by air. Charter offices, pilot accommodation and a run of practical businesses sit around it. It is functional and convenient rather than pleasant.
bestFor: Pilots, charter staff and anyone flying in and out repeatedly
pros: Airport and charter offices on the doorstep
Practical services and vehicle hire nearby

name: Boseja and the Village Side
tagline: The residential wards where Maun actually lives
description: The wards spreading south and west of the centre, where the town's Batawana population lives in family compounds among the mopane, with local shops and the everyday economy of the place. Rents are the lowest in Maun and this is where a long stay makes financial sense.
bestFor: Long stays where the rent is the deciding factor
pros: The lowest rents in the town
Genuine local community rather than a safari bubble
cons: Sandy tracks rather than roads in places
No tourist services and limited English signage

name: Okavango Delta Camps (by air, 30 to 200 km)
tagline: Inside the delta, reachable only by light aircraft or boat
description: The camps and concessions inside the delta itself, which is where the wildlife is and where almost everyone who comes to Maun is actually going. Access is by light aircraft from Maun airport or by mokoro and boat through the channels. There is no road, no grid power and no connectivity.
bestFor: Short stays inside the delta rather than any kind of base
pros: One of the great wildlife landscapes on earth
Mokoro and walking safaris from the camps
Complete disconnection, which some people want
cons: Reachable only by air or boat, at real cost
Camp pricing is in dollars and is high
